addedRecord.canonicalName: 2020-06 - EGLE Summary Report - PFAS in Municipal Wastewater and Associated Residuals.pdf

verifiedFindings: EGLE summarizes a 2018 IPP PFAS initiative covering 95 municipal WWTPs and a separate statewide assessment covering 42 WWTPs and 22 biosolids land-application sites.

The report says PFOA was not detected above the applicable state water-quality values in any participating WWTP effluent and identifies PFOS as the principal regulatory driver; 31 percent of the 95 IPP WWTPs were reported as having a PFOS source and a discharge above the applicable water-quality value.

For the 42-WWTP assessment, the report gives a PFOS biosolids/sludge average of 195 micrograms per kilogram and a median of 13 micrograms per kilogram; excluding seven industrially impacted samples reduces the stated average to 16 and median to 11 micrograms per kilogram.

Field screening found higher PFAS concentrations across environmental matrices associated with more highly impacted biosolids, while emphasizing that site-specific environmental conditions affected potential impacts and exposure pathways.
evidentiaryBoundary: The report is statewide program and technical context. Its maps and plots do not identify Cadillac or Wexford, and it supplies no Cadillac-specific sample result, delivery record, violation finding, source determination, groundwater direction or source-to-receptor pathway proof.

queueResolution.reason: The report does not supply the Cadillac-specific synchronized influent, effluent and biosolids data; complete receptor work order; receiving history; certified well construction; water-level or hydraulic-test data; or source-to-receptor sampling required by the remaining queue.
